# `net` standard library

The `net` module provides POSIX socket wrappers for TCP and UDP communication on Linux systems.
The submodule `net/http` provides HTTP protocol parsing, header manipulation, and response generation.

```dva
#use net
#use net/http
```

## Socket operations

Socket helpers return recoverable `< T | String >` ramifications rather than poisonous abort errors.

```dva
#use net

// Create a listening TCP socket on port 8080
sock = net::socket(net::AF_INET, net::SOCK_STREAM, 0)
sock
   | fd =>
      net::bind(fd, "0.0.0.0", 8080)
      net::listen(fd, 128)
   | err =>
      io::err("Socket error: " + err)
```

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `net::socket` | `Int, Int, Int => < Int \| String >` | Creates socket file descriptor |
| `net::bind` | `Int, String, Int => < () \| String >` | Binds socket to IPv4 address and port |
| `net::listen` | `Int, Int => < () \| String >` | Sets listening backlog capacity |
| `net::accept` | `Int => < (Int, String, Int) \| String >` | Accepts client connection: `(client_fd, client_ip, client_port)` |
| `net::connect` | `Int, String, Int => < () \| String >` | Connects to remote IPv4 host and port |
| `net::send` | `Int, String => < Int \| String >` | Sends string bytes over socket |
| `net::recv` | `Int, Int => < String \| String >` | Reads up to `count` bytes into string |
| `net::close` | `Int => ()` | Closes socket descriptor |
| `net::set_nonblocking` | `Int => < () \| String >` | Toggles non-blocking socket flag (`O_NONBLOCK`) |

## HTTP protocol support (`net/http`)

The `net/http` submodule parses HTTP/1.1 requests and formats responses without requiring external dependencies:

```dva
#use net/http

req = "GET /index.html?v=1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n"
path = http::path_of(req) // "/index.html"

// Construct standard HTTP response
res = http::response(200, "text/plain", "Hello, World!")
```

- `http::path_of(req: String) => String`: Extracts the normalized request target path.
- `http::reason_of(code: Int) => String`: Maps status code (e.g. `200`, `404`) to reason phrase (`"OK"`, `"Not Found"`).
- `http::header(name: String, value: String) => String`: Generates `Name: Value\r\n` line.
- `http::response(status: Int, content_type: String, body: String) => String`: Constructs complete HTTP message with `Content-Length`.
- `http::respond(fd: Int, status: Int, content_type: String, body: String) => ()`: Directly writes HTTP response to client socket.
